A Bloomberg report yesterday pointed out that the future product line of Apple Watch may undergo considerable changes.

The report specifically mentioned that Apple is exploring the launch of one or more models featuring a circular dial instead of a square one……

Most smartwatches are circular

Although square-faced watches have existed for over a century, traditional watches are mostly circular, and the same goes for Android smartwatches. Examples include:

  • Amazfit Active Max
  • Samsung Galaxy Watch 9
  • Motorola Moto Watch
  • All Garmin models (Venu, Epix Pro, Forerunner, Fenix)
  • Google Pixel Watch

Apple's choice of a rectangular design can be said to be unconventional, so it would not be surprising for them to consider launching a circular Apple Watch in the future.

The case for a circular Apple Watch

The reason Apple originally chose a rectangular design was because it could display more information. The other screens we use—phones, tablets, laptops, monitors, and so on—are all rectangular, which is no coincidence.

Ultimately, this choice is really a trade-off between aesthetics and practicality. Some people will always put practicality first, so the rectangular Apple Watch design certainly will not disappear. But there are also those who place great importance on appearance, and many people do indeed have a strong preference for circular watches—whether traditional or smart.

Besides, not everyone who wears an Apple Watch needs to see a lot of information on the screen. Even if you are not constantly checking the screen, there are plenty of good reasons to wear an Apple Watch, such as:

  • Health and fitness monitoring
  • Sleep tracking
  • Emergency features, such as fall detection
  • Contactless payment

Among the above points, health and fitness monitoring is the main attraction for many people. If you mainly do not use your Apple Watch as a device for viewing content, then a circular screen may already be more than sufficient for you.

However, the case for an Apple Ring is even stronger

However, if you are this type of user—primarily using your Apple Watch for health and fitness monitoring and basically not using it to view information—I would argue that a smart ring is the more… sensible choice.

I personally switched from the Apple Watch to an Oura smart ring in 2024, and recently upgraded to the fifth generation. I love how understated it is, that I can keep wearing the traditional watch I like, and that it only needs to be charged once a week.

Nearly two years ago, I already came out in full support of smart rings as an alternative to the Apple Watch, and argued that Apple should launch such a product. To this day, my view has not changed, and Gurman also pointed out that Eddy Cue is also a fan of smart rings, showing that this possibility is quite high.

I do think it's possible that Apple will launch a circular Apple Watch model, but I am more inclined to believe that we will see an Apple Ring. What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
